differences.title: 1. DATA AGGREGATION
differences.leftDesc: BFF aggregates and transforms data from multiple microservices into a single response.
differences.rightDesc: Frontend directly calls multiple microservices, often leading to over/under-fetching.

differences.title: 2. OPTIMIZATION
differences.leftDesc: Tailors API responses for specific frontend needs, improving performance and user experience.
differences.rightDesc: Provides generic endpoints that might not be ideal for all clients.

differences.title: 3. COMPLEXITY MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: Hides the complexity of backend microservices from the frontend, simplifying development.
differences.rightDesc: Frontend developers must manage the complexity of interacting with multiple services.

differences.title: 4. DEVELOPMENT SPEED
differences.leftDesc: Frontend teams can iterate faster without backend service changes, thanks to BFF's tailored APIs.
differences.rightDesc: Frontend development can be slower due to dependency on backend service changes.

differences.title: 5. NETWORK CHATTE
differences.leftDesc: Minimizes the number of network calls from the frontend to the backend.
differences.rightDesc: Can lead to a high number of network requests for a single view.

differences.title: 6. RESILIENCE
differences.leftDesc: Can implement fallback strategies or graceful degradation for backend service failures.
differences.rightDesc: Frontend is more susceptible to failures in individual backend services.

differences.title: 7. MAINTENANCE
differences.leftDesc: BFFs are managed independently, allowing for specific updates and maintenance.
differences.rightDesc: Changes might require coordination across multiple teams and services.
